title: The universal isomorphism locus for a diagram of algebraic spaces is open
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $A,C,B$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:A\to B$, $q:C\to B$, and $f:A\to C$ satisfy $q\circ f=p$. Use the chartwise and topological morphism properties of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]: locally of finite presentation, flat and locally of finite type are tested on etale scheme charts; separated means the diagonal is representable by closed immersions; universally closed means closed on underlying point spaces after every algebraic-space base change. A closed map means that the induced map of point spaces sends closed subsets to closed subsets. Assume that $p$ is locally of finite presentation, flat and universally closed, and that $q$ is locally of finite type, closed and separated. Then there exists an open subspace $U\subseteq B$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace] such that, for every algebraic space $B'$ over $S$ and morphism $h:B'\to B$, $h$ factors through $U$ if and only if $f_{B'}:A\times_BB'\to C\times_BB'$ is an isomorphism. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. In particular, if $B$ is a scheme, $U$ is represented by an open subscheme of $B$.

source.place: Tag 05XD, spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-where-isomorphism, all six hypotheses and arbitrary algebraic-space base-change conclusion.

proof.text: The universal closedness of $p$ includes the identity base change, so $p$ is closed. Also $p$ is locally of finite type: on every compatible etale scheme chart its finite-presentation affine description is $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$, generated over $R$ by the images of the $n$ variables. Thus the same charts satisfy local finite type. This uses only the definitions, and imposes no quasi-compactness or finite presentation on $q$.

source.place: Tag 05XD, preparation for the applications of Tags 05XC and 05XA; elementary implications of the hypotheses

proof.text: Apply the universal surjective-flat locus theorem to $(p,q,f)$. Its five hypotheses are: local finite presentation and flatness of $p$ from the assumptions, closedness of $p$ from step 1, and local finite type and closedness of $q$ from the assumptions. Obtain an open subspace $V_1\subseteq B$ such that every algebraic-space map $h:T\to B$ factors through $V_1$ exactly when $f_T$ is surjective and flat.

source.place: Tag 05XD, first sentence of the proof, applying Tag 05XC

proof.text: Apply the universal closed-immersion locus theorem to the same diagram. Its hypotheses hold because $p$ is locally of finite type by step 1 and universally closed by assumption, while $q$ is separated by assumption. Obtain an open subspace $V_2\subseteq B$ such that every algebraic-space map $h:T\to B$ factors through $V_2$ exactly when $f_T$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 05XD, second sentence of the proof, applying Tag 05XA

proof.text: Define the subfunctor $U=V_1\cap V_2\subseteq B$ by $U(R)=V_1(R)\cap V_2(R)$ inside $B(R)$ for every $S$-scheme $R$. After any scheme test $R\to B$, this is the intersection of the two open subschemes representing $R\times_BV_1$ and $R\times_BV_2$, hence is again an open subscheme of $R$. Thus $U$ is an open subspace by definition. A map $h:T\to B$ of algebraic spaces factors through $U$ if and only if it factors through both $V_1$ and $V_2$: the two lifts, viewed as natural transformations, assign to each section of $T$ an element of each subfunctor with the same image in $B$, hence an element of their intersection, naturally in $R$.

source.place: Tag 05XD, intersection W = W_1 intersect W_2; explicit subfunctor construction

proof.text: Fix any algebraic-space map $h:T\to B$. If it factors through $U$, steps 2--4 show that $f_T$ is surjective, flat and a closed immersion; the algebraic-space closed-immersion criterion [lem-sfb-space-surjective-flat-closed-immersion-isomorphism] makes $f_T$ an isomorphism. Conversely, suppose $f_T:A_T\to C_T$ is an isomorphism. Its point map is a bijection, so it is surjective on point sets. Every scheme base change $A_T\times_{C_T}R\to R$ is an isomorphism, hence represented by a scheme and a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], so $f_T$ is a representable closed immersion. For flatness, which [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] tests on every chart diagram, choose a surjective representable etale map $V\to C_T$ from a scheme [def-trf-algebraic-space]; the base change $A_T\times_{C_T}V\to V$ is an isomorphism, so $U=V$ with the inverse isomorphism is a surjective etale chart of $A_T\times_{C_T}V$, and the induced scheme map $U\to V$ is $\mathrm{id}_V$, which is flat. The chart criterion [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] for the property flat then gives that $f_T$ is flat. Steps 2 and 3 then give both factorizations, so step 4 gives the factorization through $U$. This proves the required equivalence for arbitrary algebraic spaces $T$, including nonreduced and non-scheme ones.

source.place: Tag 05XD, final paragraph and the universal equivalence

proof.text: When $B$ is a scheme, apply the defining scheme-test property of the open subspace $U\subseteq B$ to the identity $B\to B$. It represents $B\times_BU=U$ by an open subscheme of $B$, proving the final assertion.
